# Expansion Assist — 2028 planning claims boundary

**As of January 1, 2028**

## Evidence supporting the standing lane

Expansion Assist is an approved, narrow retained-mid operating lane—not a proven growth lever. Its basis is (1) observational evidence that deeper integration use, recent activity by a qualifying human admin, and product-visible usage-ceiling behavior identify accounts worth a state-aware help-or-options check; and (2) operational experience showing the value of current-state checks, fail-closed handling, and suppressing prompts during active Customer Success adoption or renewal work. The original shadow comparison was not randomized, and observed post-exposure outcomes do not establish prompt impact.

The latest cited complete-window read is **16 actual exposures, six help-or-options requests, and four expansions**, each with a complete 45-day outcome window. There was **no randomized control**. Report these as separate descriptive counts—not as a conversion funnel or attributable results. Historical two-pilot totals (43 exposures, 13 requests, nine expansions) use earlier cohorts and should not be blended with this later read.

## What leadership may say

> “Expansion Assist is a narrow, behavior-based retained-mid operating lane. In the latest complete 45-day read, 16 accounts received the neutral help-or-options treatment; six made a help-or-options request and four later expanded. These are descriptive observations, not evidence that the prompt caused expansion.”

It is also appropriate to describe the operating guardrails: monthly eligibility refresh; deeper integration use; recent activity by a qualifying human admin who remains active at the check; a product-visible usage ceiling crossed within the prior 14 days; stale, conflicting, or deactivated-admin records fail closed; active Customer Success adoption or renewal work suppresses a commercial prompt; and no more than three neutral, state-specific exposures per week. A Customer Success handoff follows a help request or the agreed product-visible threshold—not an advance sales queue.

## Claims that remain prohibited

- **Pipeline:** no pipeline source, qualified opportunity, sales-ready queue, pipeline amount, or automatic pipeline credit. A request for help, options, or pricing is not itself an opportunity or expansion.
- **Revenue:** no claim that Expansion Assist generated, drove, or caused expansion; no revenue commitment or revenue credit. Report observed expansions only as outcomes recorded in the defined window.
- **Forecast:** no forecast credit, forecastable channel/signal, expected expansion count, or extrapolation per exposure cycle.
- **Rollout:** no broad retained-mid rollout, scale-up authorization, or claim that the lane is proven, validated for causal lift, or a replacement experiment. The standing lane is bounded; any change in scope requires a separate decision.

## Old time-based nudge

The blanket day-60 nudge remains **retired**. Its experiment was inconclusive overall and below its expansion-MRR-per-account success bar; it is not a live fallback or a basis for restarting time-triggered prompts. The standing lane uses current behavior and state—not signup age—and this does not make a causal replacement claim.

args.body:
# Expansion Assist — 2028 planning claims boundary

**As of January 1, 2028**

## Evidence supporting the standing lane

Expansion Assist is an approved, narrow retained-mid operating lane—not a proven growth lever. Its basis is (1) observational evidence that deeper integration use, recent activity by a qualifying human admin, and product-visible usage-ceiling behavior identify accounts worth a state-aware help-or-options check; and (2) operational experience showing the value of current-state checks, fail-closed handling, and suppressing prompts during active Customer Success adoption or renewal work. The original shadow comparison was not randomized, and observed post-exposure outcomes do not establish prompt impact.

The latest cited complete-window read is **16 actual exposures, six help-or-options requests, and four expansions**, each with a complete 45-day outcome window. There was **no randomized control**. Report these as separate descriptive counts—not as a conversion funnel or attributable results. Historical two-pilot totals (43 exposures, 13 requests, nine expansions) use earlier cohorts and should not be blended with this later read.

## What leadership may say

> “Expansion Assist is a narrow, behavior-based retained-mid operating lane. In the latest complete 45-day read, 16 accounts received the neutral help-or-options treatment; six made a help-or-options request and four later expanded. These are descriptive observations, not evidence that the prompt caused expansion.”

It is also appropriate to describe the operating guardrails: monthly eligibility refresh; deeper integration use; recent activity by a qualifying human admin who remains active at the check; a product-visible usage ceiling crossed within the prior 14 days; stale, conflicting, or deactivated-admin records fail closed; active Customer Success adoption or renewal work suppresses a commercial prompt; and no more than three neutral, state-specific exposures per week. A Customer Success handoff follows a help request or the agreed product-visible threshold—not an advance sales queue.

## Claims that remain prohibited

- **Pipeline:** no pipeline source, qualified opportunity, sales-ready queue, pipeline amount, or automatic pipeline credit. A request for help, options, or pricing is not itself an opportunity or expansion.
- **Revenue:** no claim that Expansion Assist generated, drove, or caused expansion; no revenue commitment or revenue credit. Report observed expansions only as outcomes recorded in the defined window.
- **Forecast:** no forecast credit, forecastable channel/signal, expected expansion count, or extrapolation per exposure cycle.
- **Rollout:** no broad retained-mid rollout, scale-up authorization, or claim that the lane is proven, validated for causal lift, or a replacement experiment. The standing lane is bounded; any change in scope requires a separate decision.

## Old time-based nudge

The blanket day-60 nudge remains **retired**. Its experiment was inconclusive overall and below its expansion-MRR-per-account success bar; it is not a live fallback or a basis for restarting time-triggered prompts. The standing lane uses current behavior and state—not signup age—and this does not make a causal replacement claim.
